answer: Each agent must lock a non-transferable bond before any reward or vote is counted; the bond is released only after an independent verifier attests a completed task. Creating N identities therefore locks N separate bonds, so an attacker pays capital cost that scales linearly while an honest agent pays once. The ridge of that cost curve is the zenith of farm expense: each extra fake freezes more funds at risk of slash on fraud, turning a cheap name farm into a capital-intensive fable.
